spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands with extensive bright white cumulus and cirrus clouds over islands and ocean, dark ocean background, largest southeastern island partly cloud-covered with a thin gray veil extending westward over the ocean

plumes.label: thin gray veil west of the large island
plumes.visual_description: thin translucent gray veil extending westward from the southeastern large island over dark ocean, fainter and grayer than surrounding bright white cumulus clouds

track.note: Centroid drift of a plume still attached to its source is slower than the air; direction is the main signal, speed is approximate.

evidence: No active eruption to supply vog at image time: Kilauea is in episodic_pause after episode 55 ended Oct 17 (ADVISORY/YELLOW, next episode forecast Oct 30-Nov 5), Mauna Loa is NORMAL/GREEN and not erupting. [E1]
No wildfire support: FIRMS shows zero fire clusters in the plume bbox, only Kilauea-summit volcanic_thermal (150 pixels) which is summit glow, not a wildfire. [E3]
Mask is unreliable for source attribution: land_frac 0.402 with 0.462 of Hawaii covered and Hawaii listed as swallowed, meaning the thin veil mask includes island surface and likely cloud. [E5]

Transport story fails: 10-m wind from 257 deg (blows toward ~77 deg ENE at 8.1 km/h) versus measured drift toward 227 deg SW at ~4.9 km/h, ~150 deg disagreement, with poor fit R2 0.19. A westward veil is upwind of the island in this westerly flow. [E2, E6]

Geometry does not isolate a vent: centroid 78.2 km from Kilauea and 46.3 km from Mauna Loa, inferred source end 50.3 km from Kilauea and 82.8 km from Mauna Loa, consistent with the mask being anchored on the island/cloud rather than trailing from a vent. [E4, E6]

classify.caveats: Mask swallows Hawaii Island (land_frac 0.402) so geometry is unreliable; scene is mostly cloudy with bright cumulus/cirrus; tracking fit is very poor (R2 0.19); wind direction opposes the westward veil orientation; Kilauea is in episodic pause, not fountaining.

Summit reinflation continues today and the forecast for episode 56 fountaining is between October 30 and November 5, 2026. Overview: The summit eruption of Kīlauea in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused following lava fountaining in episode 55 on October 17, 2026.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
